To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AL2 ORF is essential for replication and spread of the virus, the AL1 ORF may be dispensible for replication, and the AL4 ORFs is not required for replication and spread.
the AL2 and BR1 ORFs are not essential for PYMV DNA replication and that the AL3 ORFs are essential.
Mutations in AL1, AL3, AL2 and AR1 ORFs resulted in attenuated infections of N. benthamian plants and that the AL2 and AL3 ORF mutations reduced DNA replication of PYMV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes and their products which are essential for geminivirus replication and symptom expression.
the identification of genes involved in the replication and spread of the virus.
understanding the function of the various genes and gene products encoded by the DNA A and B genome components of a plant geminivirus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AL1 and AL2 ORFs are essential for infectivity, and the AR1, AL3 and AL4 ORFs play an accessory role in the infectivity of PYMV.
, in contrast to other geminivirusalphavirus systems, PYMV is unable to replicate or spread independently of the DNA B component.

the AL2 and BR1 ORFs are essential for infectivity of both DNA A (PYMV) and DNA A (PYM) in both plants and leaf discs, whereas AL3 and AR1 are essential for infecting N. clevelandii plants but are not essential for infecting leaf discs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the geminivirus replication strategy is very similar to that for other DNA viruses, and that geminivirial genes involved in replication and movement are conserved.
the AL1, AL3 and BR1 ORFs are required for infectivity of PYMV.
the AL3 and AR1 ORFs appear to be important for the efficient replication of PYMV DNA in both whole plants as well as in leaf discs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AL2 gene is dispensable for replication of the PYMV genome, and the AL3 gene plays a major role in the replication of the PY MV genome.
the PYMV DNA A component is capable of independent replication in plants and that this replication can occur in the absence of a DNA B component.

, although the DNA A components of the two geminiviridae families are very similar in sequence and organization, there is considerable variation in the functions of the encoded proteins, particularly the replication proteins.
